 In Practice: Have your say at RACGP AGM 
 Morgan Liotta 
 29/10/2026 4:23:23 PM 
 Members are invited to vote in the upcoming Annual General Meeting in person or online, to ensure the college is set up for the future. 
 Voting in the RACGP’s 2026 AGM will open for eligible members on 9 November. 
 This week’s  In Practice  also includes updates on TGA sunscreen reforms and consultation outcomes, and an educational event on prevention of congenital cytomegalovirus.
 RACGP AGM   2026 
The RACGP’s 69th Annual General Meeting (AGM) will be held on Thursday 19 November at 5.00 pm (ACDT) / 5.30 pm (AEDT) at GP26 and live streamed online.  
By attending, RACGP members can engage directly with the Board and ask questions about the college’s activities and financial performance for the last financial year. Eligible members will vote on resolutions to ensure the college can continue advocating for the profession, while remaining accountable to members and responsive to their needs. 
Voting will open for eligible members on 9 November at 12.00 pm (AEDT). 
 Register to attend and review the resolutions online .
 Update on TGA sunscreen reforms 
The Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) has published the consultation outcomes and updates for sunscreen reforms. Together with the published submissions, these can be accessed on the consultation hub .
The TGA says the reforms to sunscreen regulation being developed are intended to ‘strengthen consumer confidence in sunscreen performance and ensure that sunscreen sponsors and manufacturers understand their regulatory obligations’.
The TGA’s sunscreen reforms page will continue to be updated as the reforms progress and further information becomes available. Healthcare professionals can monitor this page for the latest updates on implementation activities, guidance, and future reform milestones.
 Prevention of congenital CMV infection 
 Webinar : Monday 23 November, 7.00 pm (AEDT)
 Register online 
The Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG) is hosting a webinar on the recently updated Prevention of congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection (C-Obs 64) statement .
The 2026 interim update to the CMV statement was undertaken to address areas requiring immediate alignment with Australian, New Zealand and international guidance, and the priorities of people with lived experience of CMV in pregnancy. To support the implementation of these important updates, the webinar will feature an expert multidisciplinary panel that will discuss the key changes to the statement and its application within clinical care.
